question: In light of the farmers’ protests in Greece, the National Union of Agricultural Cooperatives (ETHEAS) issued a communication1in which it raised the issue of amending the CAP eco-schemes. The association had already expressed its reservations regarding the application and applicability of the eco-schemes in a letter it addressed to the relevant minister last November2.

Given that eco-schemes are an essential building block of the Green Architecture concept under the first pillar of the CAP 2023-27 and that the eco-schemes chosen by the Member States were approved by the relevant Commission services when the National Strategic Plan was submitted, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Was there an assessment of the relevance of the eco-schemes in relation to the objectives of the CAP's Green Architecture, as well as an assessment of how feasible it is for Greek farmers to apply the schemes, and is the schemes’ implementation status being monitored?
Is consideration being given to the possibility of the Commission lending its expertise so that the eco-schemes can be completed in a timely and reliable manner?
Is the payment of relevant subsidies to beneficiaries, as provided for under the institutional framework, monitored?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.3.2024) The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) Strategic Plans (CSPs) are established by Member States and approved by the Commission to ensure that amongst other, they contribute to climate action, protecting natural resources and halting and reversing biodiversity loss.

Member States used the CAP instruments, including eco-schemes, to design their intervention strategies for each objective based on the analyses of strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats on their respective territories, and their related needs. After receiving the CSPs the Commission issued observations to the Member States1, that led to revisions and final approval of the CSPs by the end of 20222.

The Commission monitors the implementation of the Greek CSP through participating in the work of the Greek monitoring committee, the annual performance report, the annual review meeting, and other working interactions. The preliminary information on uptake of CSP interventions in Greece shows a substantial interest by farmers for the eco-schemes.

On request of a Member State, the Commission may provide technical assistance. Examples of best practices are shared on a regular basis with all Member States, mainly through the activities of the EU CAP network3.

A specific thematic group on design and implementation of eco-schemes has been running from October 2023 to February 2024 with two meetings and intermediate exchanges covering most of managing authorities, including Greece, and numerous stakeholders.

As regards the monitoring of payments, the Commission follows the progress through the declaration of expenditure per intervention, that Greece submits by the seventh day of each month and by the annual clearance of accounts procedures.
